name: pixel-world
//: Read the comment in .devcontainer/Dockerfile first. Containment here is a function of what is NOT mounted and NOT installed, so the mount list below is deliberately short. Before adding a mount, ask: does this need to be writable, does it carry a credential, and is there a path that does not require it? For the history: the lab containers in ~/lab mount more because they also need the bot PAT, msmtp, and the host tool directory for docker workflows; this repo needs none of those. Adding a mount here is a security decision, not a convenience one.
//mounts-why: Four mounts, and each is deliberate. (1) the repo-scoped PAT, mounted to the same relative path it has on the host so git-askpass.sh needs no container-specific variant. NOT the ~/.config/jef directory — that would also expose the jefscad PAT once it exists. (2) and (3) the shared instruction files, read-only so the agent cannot edit the rules it is operating under. (4) the wiki, read-only: the agent reads the distilled kb fundamentals, this project's implementation pages, and other projects' pages when a decision has cross-project implications — but cannot write, because the wiki is the one tier where an undetected error compounds instead of being caught. Proposals go to notes/wiki-proposals/ and a human promotes them (see wiki-sync.md). NOT ~/.ssh (the personal key reaches every repo on the account, including the wiki), NOT ~/.config/lab-bot (the bot credential), NOT ~/.aws or ~/.azure, NOT the host tool directory, NOT the docker socket (this repo builds nothing locally — its images, if any, are not its business).

remoteEnv.//git: GIT_ASKPASS points at the tracked script that reads the mounted PAT. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 stops a failed lookup from falling back to an interactive prompt, which in an unattended run hangs until the run is killed. GIT_SSH_COMMAND=/bin/false is a second line of defence behind the missing ssh binary: even if one is added later, git cannot silently fall back to SSH.
